activity.overview: Show what you know about DNA, protein synthesis and mutations. You may use the codon table.

problems.prompt: State the base-pairing rules for DNA with DNA and for DNA with RNA. Then give three differences between DNA and RNA.
Explain why DNA replication is called semiconservative. If one original strand reads TAGGC, what is the sequence of the new strand built on it?
A DNA template strand reads TAC CAT GGG TTT ATC. Write the mRNA and the amino acid sequence.
In the gene from problem 3, the second template codon changes from CAT to CTT. What happens to the mRNA and the protein? Classify the mutation.
A muscle cell and a nerve cell from the same person have exactly the same DNA, yet they look and work very differently. Explain how this is possible.

Put these events of protein synthesis in order and say where each happens: a tRNA anticodon pairs with a codon; mRNA leaves the nucleus; a stop codon is reached; the DNA of a gene unzips; amino acids are joined by a peptide bond; mRNA is built from the template strand.
A sample of DNA is 30% adenine. What percentage of the bases are thymine, guanine and cytosine? Show your reasoning.

activity.title: DNA and Proteins Check

readings.body:
Read each mRNA codon (three bases) from left to right, starting at the start codon AUG. These are the codons you need for this unit; the full table has 64.

Start: AUG = Met (methionine), which also begins every protein
Ala (alanine): GCU, GCC, GCA, GCG
Glu (glutamic acid): GAA, GAG
Gly (glycine): GGU, GGC, GGA, GGG
His (histidine): CAU, CAC
Ile (isoleucine): AUU, AUC, AUA
Leu (leucine): CUU, CUC, CUA, CUG, UUA, UUG
Lys (lysine): AAA, AAG
Phe (phenylalanine): UUU, UUC
Pro (proline): CCU, CCC, CCA, CCG
Ser (serine): UCU, UCC, UCA, UCG, AGU, AGC
Thr (threonine): ACU, ACC, ACA, ACG
Trp (tryptophan): UGG
Val (valine): GUU, GUC, GUA, GUG
Stop (end of the protein): UAA, UAG, UGA

Base-pairing rules. DNA to DNA: A pairs with T, G pairs with C. DNA template to mRNA: A to U, T to A, G to C, C to G.
